title: Consumer
text: Consumer means a person who buys goods or hires or avails services for consideration, subject to the statutory exclusions and conditions in the Act.

title: Complaint
text: Complaint means an allegation made in writing by a complainant seeking relief under the Act in relation to matters such as unfair trade practice, defective goods, deficiency in services, overcharging, or other grounds covered by the Act.

title: Defect
text: Defect means a fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, purity or standard of goods that is required by law, contract or representation.

title: Deficiency
text: Deficiency means a fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of performance of a service required by law, contract or otherwise.

title: Misleading Advertisement
text: The Act defines misleading advertisement to include advertisements that falsely describe a product or service, give a false guarantee, convey a misleading representation, or deliberately conceal important information, subject to the statutory definition.

title: Service
text: Service includes service of any description made available to potential users and includes banking, financing, insurance, transport, processing, supply of electrical or other energy, telecom and similar services, subject to statutory exclusions.

title: Unfair Trade Practice
text: Unfair trade practice covers specified unfair or deceptive methods used to promote the sale, use or supply of goods or services, including specified false representations and other conduct listed in the Act.

title: Central Consumer Protection Authority
text: The Act establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of consumer rights, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements and to protect and enforce consumer rights as provided by the Act.

title: Powers and Functions of CCPA
text: The Central Authority has statutory functions including protecting and enforcing consumer rights, preventing unfair trade practices, preventing false or misleading advertisements, and investigating or inquiring into violations within its powers.

title: Recall and Reimbursement Powers
text: The Central Authority may order recall of dangerous, hazardous or unsafe goods, withdrawal of unsafe services, reimbursement of prices paid by consumers and discontinuance of practices prejudicial to consumers, subject to the Act.

title: False or Misleading Advertisements
text: The Central Authority may direct a person to discontinue or modify a false or misleading advertisement and may impose statutory penalties in circumstances covered by the Act.

title: Jurisdiction of District Commission
text: The District Consumer Commission has jurisdiction over complaints within the statutory pecuniary and territorial framework prescribed by the Act and applicable rules.

title: Manner of Making Complaint
text: A complaint concerning goods or services may be filed before the appropriate District Commission by a consumer, a recognised consumer association, or other persons/entities specified by the Act.

title: Proceedings Before District Commission
text: The District Commission is to follow the statutory procedure for admission and hearing of consumer complaints and related proceedings under the Act.

title: Opposite Party Version
text: After admission of a complaint, the District Commission refers a copy to the opposite party and directs the opposite party to give its version within thirty days or such extended period not exceeding fifteen days as may be granted.

title: Findings and Orders
text: Where the District Commission finds that goods have a defect or a service has a deficiency, or another statutory ground is established, it may grant one or more remedies specified by the Act, including repair, replacement, refund or compensation where applicable.

title: Appeal Against District Commission Order
text: A person aggrieved by an order of a District Commission may appeal to the State Commission within the statutory period and subject to the conditions prescribed by the Act.

title: Jurisdiction of State Commission
text: The State Commission exercises the appellate and original jurisdiction assigned to it by the Act, including complaints and appeals within the statutory framework.

title: Jurisdiction of National Commission
text: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission exercises original, appellate and revisional jurisdiction as provided by the Act and applicable statutory limits.

title: Limitation Period
text: A complaint must ordinarily be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose, subject to the statutory power to condone delay for sufficient cause when the requirements of the Act are met.
